central-valley.caption: USGS's famous pole near Mendota: the signs mark the ground level in 1925, 1955 and 1977. That's about 9 m (28 ft) of sinking, all from pumping groundwater.
central-valley.title: SanJoaquinDrop.jpg
central-valley.author: USGS (unknown photographer)

central-valley.caption: NASA JPL radar map of land sinking and rising across California. The Central Valley bowls really stand out.
central-valley.title: Map of California Subsidence and Uplift (PIA25530).jpg
central-valley.author: NASA Earth Observatory
central-valley.credit: This image or video was catalogued by Jet Propulsion Laboratory of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: PIA25530.

norfolk.caption: Hurricane Isabel floods parking at Naval Station Norfolk, September 2003. As the ground sinks and the sea rises, water like this reaches further.
norfolk.title: US Navy 030918-N-3235P-018 Rain and heavy winds from Hurricane Isabel flooded portions of Fleet Parking at Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia.jpg
norfolk.author: U.S. Navy photo by Photographer’s Mate 1st Class Michael Pendergrass.
norfolk.credit: This image was released by the United States Navy with the ID 030918-N-3235P-018 (next). This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required.

jakarta.caption: Fishermen in Muara Baru, North Jakarta, walk home along the sea wall. It was built because the land behind it now sits below the sea.
jakarta.title: Pulang dari Laut.jpg
jakarta.author: Yohaneshsh7342

jakarta.caption: Flooded streets in Jakarta, January 2013. Sinking ground makes floods deeper and slower to drain.
jakarta.title: VOA People walk through Jakarta's flooded streets.jpg
jakarta.author: VOA Indonesian Service
jakarta.credit: Voice of America: Flooded Jakarta Braces for More Downpours

mexico-city.caption: NISAR's own map of Mexico City sinking (NASA/JPL-Caltech, 2026): the same L-band radar this app is built around.
mexico-city.title: US-Indian Spacecraft Captures Mexico City Subsidence (PIA26709).jpg
mexico-city.author: NASA/JPL-Caltech/David Bekaert
mexico-city.credit: This image or video was catalogued by Jet Propulsion Laboratory of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: PIA26709.

mexico-city.caption: Our Lady of Loreto, Mexico City, 1986: the church is slightly tilted by ground subsidence as the lakebed clay beneath it compacts.
mexico-city.title: Ciudad de México, calles y plazas 1986 07.jpg
mexico-city.author: LBM1948

svartsengi.caption: Sundhnúkur crater ringed by fresh lava, August 2024, with the Svartsengi power plant behind.
svartsengi.title: Sundhnúkur 2024 (0734).jpg
svartsengi.author: Steinninn

svartsengi.caption: Grindavík and the Reykjanes coast from a plane, April 2025, after the Sundhnúkur eruptions.
svartsengi.title: 2025 Grindavik volcanic eruption aftermath aerial view.jpg
svartsengi.author: Manticorp

kilauea.caption: Fissure 8 erupting in Leilani Estates on 28 June 2018 (USGS). This is the vent that fed the lava flow to Kapoho.
kilauea.title: Kilauea Fissure 8 cone erupting on 6-28-2018.jpg
kilauea.author: United States Geological Survey

kilauea.caption: Lava pours into Kapoho Bay on 4 June 2018 and buries the homes around it (USGS). You can see this same bay before and after in Then & Now.
kilauea.title: Kapoho Bay lava 20180604.jpg
kilauea.author: US Geological Survey

san-andreas.caption: A curb in Hollister pulled out of line by fault creep, the slow and quiet slip that radar can measure from space.
san-andreas.title: San Andreas Fault Aseismic Creep.jpg
san-andreas.author: USGS

campi-flegrei.caption: The Roman 'Serapeum' in Pozzuoli. Marine shells bored into these columns when the ground sank below the sea. They keep a 2,000-year record of the caldera rising and falling.
campi-flegrei.title: Serapeum (Pozzuoli) -1.jpg
campi-flegrei.author: Ferdinando Marfella
campi-flegrei.credit: originally posted to Flickr as Pozzuoli

kahramanmaras.caption: Antakya from the air, May 2023, three months after the M 7.8 and M 7.5 earthquakes.
kahramanmaras.title: City of Antakya after 7.8 magnitude earthquake in Türkiye.jpg
kahramanmaras.author: Orhan Erkılıç (VOA)

kahramanmaras.caption: A damaged building in Antakya, February 2023.
kahramanmaras.title: A damaged building in Antakya.jpg
kahramanmaras.author: Yıldız Yazıcıoğlu (VOA)

nile-delta.caption: The Nile Delta at night from the International Space Station, March 2025 (NASA). About 39 million people live on this low fan of land between Cairo and the sea.
nile-delta.title: Egypt's Nile Delta region (iss072e905240).jpg
nile-delta.author: NASA Johnson Space Center
nile-delta.credit: This image or video was catalogued by Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: iss072e905240.

nile-delta.caption: Where the Rosetta branch of the Nile meets the Mediterranean at Rashid. Since the Aswan High Dam, the river carries very little mud down to build this coast back up.
nile-delta.title: RashidNileMouth.jpg
nile-delta.author: Roland Unger

nile-delta.caption: Alexandria's Corniche runs right along the sea. Old buildings along this coast have been collapsing far more often as salty groundwater rises beneath them.
nile-delta.title: Egypt, Alexandria, The Corniche of Alexandria, Mediterranean Sea.jpg
nile-delta.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg
